beliefs: The box reverses the order of characters in the input string [E1]
Reversal preserves case, digits, punctuation, and spaces exactly, only order changes [E1]
Exactly one leading space (0x20) is stripped from the input before reversal, if present; further leading spaces/tabs/newlines are kept [E13, E9, E11]
Trailing whitespace of all kinds is stripped from the input before reversal [E6, E7, E10, E12]
After reversal, leading whitespace of all kinds is stripped from the result [E7, E10]
Equivalently: remove one leading space, strip trailing whitespace (all kinds), reverse, then strip leading whitespace (all kinds) from the result [E13]
notes: E13 shows only a single leading space is removed (not all leading spaces), so lstrip(' ') became removing at most one leading space; the trailing strip and post-reversal lstrip still hold.
